ATOBonus.description: One Against the Odds bonus. influence, experience and reroll are plain switches (gains, count); toolKit (kits, purchase), wanderer and ambush are bonuses the app has its own windows for. Any other key is a plain bonus that costs its rating and adds its gains.

affects.description: What a re-roll may re-roll: singleDieOrSingleResult. Informational.

appliesIn.description: When the bonus acts: setup, game, aftermath or scenarioChoice. A practice match refuses the bonuses that only pay in the aftermath.

carriesOver.description: true: the bonus lasts beyond the match. Informational.

count.description: How many re-rolls the bonus gives (reroll).

gains.description: What the bonus adds after the match.

key.description: The key of the bonus; unique. influence, experience, reroll, toolKit, wanderer and ambush have their own behaviour.

kits.description: The kits of the Tool Kit bonus.

purchase.description: How many kits may be bought (Tool Kit).

rating.description: The Rating the bonus adds to the company's rating (for the Tool Kit, per kit).

temporary.description: true: the bonus lasts for one match (wanderer). Informational.

usableIn.description: Where a re-roll may be used: game or warsAftermath. Informational.

ATOBudget.description: The rule that the sum of the Ratings of the chosen bonuses may not take the lower company above its opponent's Rating.

inclusive.description: true: the bonuses may take the lower company exactly up to its opponent's Rating ("must not exceed"); false: they must leave it below.

ATOEligible.description: Who may choose bonuses: the company with the strictly lower Rating, compared before the bonuses.

company.description: lowerRating: the company that chooses. Informational.

compare.description: strictlyLower: at equal Ratings nobody chooses. Informational.

ratingBeforeBonuses.description: true: the comparison is made before the bonuses. Informational.

ATOGains.description: The rewards a bonus adds after the match.

experiencePerModel.description: Experience added for every model of the company, by result.

influence.description: Influence added for the company, by result.

ATOGrant.description: What a structured bonus gives: loaned equipment (Tool Kit), a temporary model (Wanderer) or the choice of the scenario (Ambush!). The app reads these bonuses by their key; these keys state the rules in data for the reader of the file and are not read.

addsRating.description: true: the loaned items add to the Rating.

assignAt.description: When the items are handed out: beforeSetup.

carriesOver.description: true: the grant lasts beyond the match.

count.description: How many models the grant adds.

countsTowardsBreakPoint.description: true: the temporary model counts for the Break Point.

countsTowardsMaxModels.description: true: the temporary model counts towards the company's size.

duration.description: How long the choice holds: thisMatch.

exclusiveWithPermanentWanderer.description: true: a company with a permanent Wanderer cannot take it.

from.description: Where the choice comes from (data.wanderers.items, scenarios).

gainsExperience.description: true: the temporary model earns Experience.

ignores.description: The rules the loaned items ignore: capacity, alignment.

persistsAfterMatch.description: true: the model stays after the match.

ratingCost.description: bonusRating: it costs the bonus's rating.

rolesBy.description: How the roles are given: scenarioRules.

rollsInjuries.description: true: the temporary model rolls on the injury chart.

rules.description: The rules of the temporary model in words.

stillApplies.description: The restrictions that still apply: heroOnly.

takesRosterSlot.description: true: the temporary model takes a place of the roster.

usableByTemporaryWanderer.description: true: the temporary Wanderer may use the items.

ATOKit.description: A kit of the Tool Kit bonus: the items it lends.

name.description: The name of the kit; the app makes the key of the kit from its first word (Healer's Kit is healer). Unique.

ATOKitItem.description: An item of a kit and how many copies the kit holds.

count.description: How many copies the kit holds; default 1.

equipment.description: The name of an equipment item of the file; a name with (X) asks the player for the weapon it is on.

ATOPurchase.description: How many kits the Tool Kit bonus may be bought for.

chooses.description: oneKit: each purchase is one kit.

distinctKits.description: true: a kit may be bought once. Informational; the app always refuses a kit twice.

maxPurchases.description: The most kits that may be bought.

ratingPerKit.description: true: every kit costs the bonus's rating. Informational; the Tool Kit always does.

other.description: The reward for a Draw or a Defeat.

Abilities.description: The two item abilities the engine reads; every other ability is item text only.

ActivatedBy.description: Who may use a consumable item and when.

carrier.description: hero: only a hero may use it; anyModel: any model.

fledModelIs.description: notCasualty: a model that fled the board is not a casualty. Informational.

requires.description: What must hold: participated (the model took part), casualty, notCasualty.

Adjust.description: How a player may spend Influence to move the recruiting die.

costPerPoint.description: The Influence one point of movement costs.

direction.description: up, down or both: the direction the die may be moved.

maxPerAttempt.description: The most points the die may be moved in one recruiting attempt, over both charts together.

AdvanceTo.description: A promotion target: a unit name, or {unit, with} when the promotion also gives wargear.

Advancement.description: Which units a unit may be promoted to.

to.description: The units it may become: a name, or {unit, with} when the promotion also gives wargear.

with.description: The wargear the unit must carry to be promoted.

AftermathEffect.description: A reward or bonus of the War's Aftermath: a scenario reward (kind influence, experience or freeEquipment), a consumable item (injuryRollModifier, injuryRollReplacement), a die modifier (rendezvous and vantagePoint, by key) or the effect of an Against the Odds bonus. The kind and the keys the engine acts on are listed first; the others state the rule in data for the reader of the file.

activatedBy.description: Who may use a consumable and when.

amount.description: The Influence or Experience Points a reward gives (kind influence or experience).

applies.description: eachInjuryRoll: the modifier applies to every injury roll of the company.

choice.description: player: the player decides whether to use it.

clamp.description: [low, high]: the modified injury total is held to this range.

consumes.description: oneItem or thisItem: what is used up when the effect is used.

die.description: second: the modifier moves the second die of the scenario table. Informational.

gains.description: The Influence or Experience by result of an Against the Odds bonus: win for a Victory, other for a Draw or Defeat.

ignoresWill.description: true: the power works even when the model has no Will left. Informational.

includesHealOneInjury.description: true: a Full Recovery from the effect also heals one injury. Informational.

includesHeroReroll.description: true: the modifier also applies to a hero's re-roll. Informational.

key.description: The key a scenario reward (rewards[].effect) or an item (aftermathEffect) points at; unique. rendezvous and vantagePoint also need a range.

kind.description: What the effect is. influence and experience pay a scenario reward (amount); freeEquipment lets a model take an item worth at most maxInfluenceValue; injuryRollModifier and injuryRollReplacement are consumables; reinforcementRollModifier and scenarioTableModifier move a die (rendezvous, vantagePoint); rerolls, experiencePerModel and magicalPower are rules the players apply.

maxInfluenceValue.description: freeEquipment: the most Influence the free item may cost.

modifier.description: injuryRollModifier: added to the injury total.

noRoll.description: injuryRollReplacement: true means the model does not roll on the chart.

range.description: [low, high], how far the effect moves a die; -6..6.

result.description: injuryRollReplacement: the key of the injury result the model counts as having rolled; required for that kind.

rolls.description: How many rolls the die modifier applies to.

scenario.description: The scenario the effect belongs to, as named in scenarios[].

source.description: Where the rule comes from in the rulebook, for the reader of the file.

stackable.description: false: only one of the effect counts per aftermath.

text.description: The rule in words, shown to the players.

to.description: leader: the reward goes to the Leader.

usableIn.description: Where a re-roll may be used: game or warsAftermath.

usesPerAftermath.description: How often the effect may be used in one aftermath. Informational.

when.description: When a perk or consumable is used: beforeInjuryRolls, firstReinforcementRollThisAftermath, nextScenarioTableRoll or nextGame.

who.description: Who gets the effect, in words of the data (victor, lowerRatedCompany ...). Open: the app does not read it.

AgainstTheOdds.description: The bonuses the lower rated company may take after the scenario roll, and the rules of the budget and of who may choose. The bonuses and the budget are read by the engine; the other keys are rule text.

bonuses.description: The bonuses, in the order the players see them.

budget.description: The Rating budget of the bonuses.

selectedAt.description: When the bonuses are chosen: afterScenarioRollBeforeSetup. Informational.

text.description: The rule in words. Shown to the players.

ArmourUpgrade.description: The rule "Upgrade Armour by one stage": the names of each stage, lowest first, and what an upgrade costs.

gold.description: The Gold one upgrade costs; default the rating.

stages.description: The names of each stage, lowest first; a list of lists of equivalent names.

AttacksBonus.description: A bonus to Attacks that holds only in a game situation; item text, never added to the profile.

Aura.description: A ring of influence around the bearer, on a rule, an item or a magical power.

bearer.description: Hero: only a Hero bearer gets the ring.

concept.description: A glossary or rule name that resolves, for the chip's popup.

from.description: On a rule: what draws it. rule (default), heroicAction, hero or power.

group.description: The Auras dialog switch (an id of auras.groups); default: when.

items.description: On an item: other items that draw the same ring.

keywords.description: A filter on the affected models (tooltip only).

kind.description: banner, command, support, enemy or utility.

label.description: The name of this ring when it is not the owner's. The rings of one owner need different labels.

los.description: true: the ring needs line of sight (tooltip only).

mergeLabels.description: Other labels shown as this ring.

radius.description: Inches from the edge of the bearer's base.

replaces.description: Labels of the rings this one supersedes.

tip.description: One sentence shown with the entry.

when.description: always, declared, conditional, target or cast.

AuraGroup.description: A group of auras by when they apply, one switch of the Auras dialog.

AuraKind.description: A kind of aura with its colour and label.

Auras.description: The aura vocabulary tables: kinds and groups, once.

Balance.description: Says one keyword may not outnumber another in the company.

notMoreThan.description: The keyword it may not outnumber.

BreakDefault.description: The Break Point of a company that has none of its own.

of.description: What the share is taken of: startingModels.

percent.description: The share of the starting models that must be lost, as a whole percent. Write this or share.

share.description: The share of the starting models that must be lost, as a fraction that is a whole percent ("1/2"). Write this or percent.

BreakException.description: A scenario, or a scenario setting, that changes the Courage tests or the count of a Broken company. The live match of that scenario shows the text.

effect.description: What the exception does: noCourageTest, autoPassCourage, notCountedForBreakPoint or yetToArriveCountAsOnTheBattlefield.

rule.description: The name of the scenario rule that causes it, for the reader and the generated sentence.

scenario.description: The scenario the exception belongs to, spelled as in scenarios[]. Write this or scenarioSetting.

scenarioSetting.description: The scenario setting the exception belongs to: a scenario rule listed in a scenario's usesRules, such as Maelstrom of Battle; compared without case. Write this or scenario.

text.description: The sentence the live match shows. Without it the app words the exception from effect and who.

who.description: Who it concerns: modelsOnTheHill, defenderWithin6OfTheGate, defenderBaggagePonies, neutralModels or ownModelsNotArrived.

BreakPoint.description: When a company is Broken and what happens then, and the scenarios that change it.

default.description: The Break Point of a company with none of its own.

scenarioExceptions.description: The scenarios, and scenario settings, that change the Courage tests or the count of a Broken company; the live match lists them.

whenBroken.description: What happens when the company is Broken.

BreakThreshold.description: How the casualties are compared with the Break Point.

comparison.description: gt: Broken with strictly more casualties than the Break Point. gte: exactly the Break Point is Broken too. The Break Point is never rounded.

BuyUnit.description: A unit a company may recruit directly for its own Influence cost, outside the chart.

pick.description: true: the player picks the unit's options.

rare.description: Rare N: at most N of it in the roster.

unit.description: The unit, by the name the company calls it.

Campaign.description: The engine parameters and tables the app switches on: company shape, recruitment, Influence, progression, injuries, experience, the Break Point, rating and scenario selection. A value here replaces the shipped one; the ranges are checked.

aftermathEffects.description: Rewards and bonuses of the War's Aftermath, keyed by the name a scenario reward or an item points at.

againstTheOdds.description: The Against the Odds bonuses of the lower-rated company, and how the budget and the eligibility work.

characteristicLimits.description: The ceilings of the characteristics and the average profile.

gold.description: How Gold works, in the words of the file. Open data (any JSON, or absent): the app does not read it; Gold is a number on the company, from start.gold and the organiser's grants.

influence.description: The Influence of the War's Aftermath.

matchInput.description: What the players enter per match: a description for the people who read the file; the app does not read it.

options.description: The campaign options the organiser can switch. The key decides what the app does: an option key the app does not know is listed as unsupported, with a warning in the log.

CampaignOption.description: A setting the file offers the organiser of a campaign: a rule variant (scope rules) or how the app behaves (scope app). The app switches the options it knows by key and lists any other as unsupported.

default.description: true: the option is on in a new campaign.

description.description: A sentence shown under the label.

implemented.description: false: the file lists the option but the app cannot switch it on. Absent means implemented, if the app knows the key.

key.description: The key of the option; unique. The keys the app knows are heroesDropProfileGear, customOnTheirOwnPath, shakeTheTable and manualRolls.

label.description: The name the campaign form shows.

scope.description: rules: a rule variant that changes the game; app: how the app behaves.

swaps.description: For an option that puts one path in the place of another.

Casualty.description: When a composite model is injured and the injury table it rolls on.

table.description: The injury table it rolls on.

wholeModel.description: true: the whole model is lost.

CharacteristicIncrease.description: Limits on the improvements a hero adds up.

courageIntelligenceTotalCap.description: The cap on the total improvement of Courage and Intelligence.

CharacteristicLimits.description: The ceilings of the characteristics: which ones improve downwards, the highest each one goes, the average profile the hero rating starts from, and the cap on the total improvement of Courage and Intelligence.

average.description: The average value of each characteristic of a profile ({attack: 1, courage: 7 ...}); the base the hero rating counts points above. A characteristic that is absent is not counted.

increases.description: Limits on the improvements a hero adds up.

lowerIsBetter.description: The characteristics where a lower number is better (Shoot, Courage, Intelligence): an improvement lowers them and best, not max, is their limit.

peak.description: The highest each characteristic goes, whatever the path.

Chart.description: The reinforcement chart: the Influence a reinforcement costs and the rows by roll.

rows.description: The rows; together they cover the recruiting die exactly once.

ChartChoice.description: One of the units an options row lets the player pick, with the number of it the company may have.

ChartRow.description: One row of a reinforcement or special chart. A row is exactly one of: a unit, nothing, special, choose or options.

blocks.description: On a nothing row: it also blocks further rolls.

choose.description: The words of a row that lets the player take a result of the chart; needs scope.

options.description: The player picks one of these units.

pick.description: true: the player picks the unit's options.

picks.description: On a choose row, how many results the player takes (1 to 10, default 1).

rare.description: Rare N: at most N of this unit in the roster; the result is recruited as a lower one when exhausted.

roll.description: The roll the row covers: a number, "2-3" or [2, 3].

scope.description: above: the units of the rows above the roll on the chart being rolled. any: the units of any row of both charts.

special.description: The roll goes on to the special chart (reinforcement chart only).

text.description: The words of an options row.

with.description: The options or wargear the recruit comes with.

ChosenGrant.description: The rule an item grants for the weapon its bearer chooses (Envenom Weapon).

weaponClasses.description: The classes of weapon the bearer may choose.

Company.description: A Battle Company: its starting force, reinforcement and special charts, advancements, hero upgrades, own units and gear, and the rules that are its own.

advancements.description: The promotions of the company's units.

aka.description: Other spellings of the same name (true synonyms only). A spelling that already is a vanilla name is refused.

breakPoint.description: This company's own Break Point (Muster of Isengard: "33/50", 66 percent); a whole percent, as a fraction or a percent number; default campaign.breakPoint.default.

description.description: The text at the head of the company's page.

elvenWeaponry.description: The models of the company that may also buy and wear Elven-made weaponry, which is otherwise restricted to Elf models. An empty object means every model. A company's own unique wargear keeps its own who.

epigraph.description: The quote and flavour sentence that head the company's rules.

extends.description: A company of this file whose fields this one inherits where it does not write them (Elite Arnor extends Arnor). A list or object you write replaces the base's as a whole. name, faction, description, epigraph, notes and specialRules are never inherited.

faction.description: The faction keyword of the company; default the name.

gear.description: The unique wargear of this company.

granted.description: Special rules the company gives for free.

heroUpgrades.description: The Company Hero Upgrades: rules a hero may take instead of a rolled result.

heroes.description: Who may be a starting hero; recruits that join as heroes.

id.description: A stable id; default: the name as a slug. Write it only to keep an id when the name changes.

label.description: How the pages spell the name when the key is plainer (Lothlórien for Lothlorien). It must be the same name once accents, case and punctuation are folded; a different name is a different company.

limits.description: Limit exemptions, changed shares and keyword caps of this company.

maxModels.description: The most models in this company; default campaign.company.maxModels.

name.description: The name of the company; the key every chart, advancement and campaign refers to.

notes.description: Notes of the company page, placed by section.

ownPath.description: The units that are On Their Own Path.

promotions.description: Promotions to Hero for units of this company.

rules.description: Rule definitions local to this company.

specialRules.description: The sentences of the company's rules that have no typed form here; a typed object keeps its own text.

substitutions.description: Models treated as other models for a rule.

units.description: Units local to this company (an alias with extends, a composite model...). A chart, an advancement or the starting force names them.

CompanyLimit.description: The limits of one company: exemptions, changed shares and keyword caps.

company.description: No more than a share of the company may have a keyword.

exempt.description: Models or items that do not count towards limits.

override.description: A limit's own share for this company, by limit id (Osgiliath: bow "1/2"); a fraction, or a percent number converted to the exact fraction over 100.

CompanyNote.description: A note of a company page, placed by section.

section.description: The section of the page: startingCompany, reinforcements, specialChart, advancements or eliteCompany.

CompanyRules.description: The shape of a company: its size, officers, the stats of a new hero and the equipment slots.

equipmentSlots.description: The equipment slots of every model before items add any.

heroStart.description: The Might, Will and Fate a new hero starts with.

leaders.description: How many Leaders a company has.

maxModels.description: The most models in a company (a company may set its own maxModels).

oaths.description: Fallback oath texts by alignment (good and evil, each {text, vow}) for a company that has no oath of its own. {name} in the text is replaced by the company's name.

sergeants.description: How many Sergeants a company has. Leaders plus sergeants may not exceed maxModels, and the company needs at least one officer.

startingInfluence.description: The Influence a new company starts with.

Composite.description: One model on the table that counts as several for the company (the Warg Marauder: three riders on a Warg).

onePhysicalCard.description: true: one card for all parts.

rules.description: The special rules that explain how it plays.

CompositeCount.description: What a composite model counts as: roster slots and limits.

bowLimit.description: What it counts as for the bow limit.

cavalryLimit.description: What it counts as for the Cavalry limit.

slots.description: The roster slots it counts as, against the maximum.

CompositePart.description: A part of a composite model: a rider or the mount.

count.description: How many of the part; default 1.

CountGrant.description: A special rule a hero gets once it has an injury a given number of times.

CourageTest.description: The test a model of a Broken company takes.

dice.description: The dice rolled; the model passes with a total at least its Courage.

passIf.description: totalAtLeastCourage, the only pass rule the app implements. A live match refuses to roll a Courage test when it is missing.

DefenceBonus.description: The Defence a shield adds and what cancels it.

cancelledByClasses.description: Classes of item that cancel it (bow, crossbow, two_handed).

cancelledByTwoHandedUse.description: true: cancelled by a hand-and-a-half weapon used two-handed (decided per fight, only shown).

conditional.description: true: situational, so a note on the item that the Defence never includes.

DefenceLift.description: A rule that lifts a cancellation of a Defence bonus.

DiceGrant.description: Experience or Influence rolled on a die.

DiceSpec.description: A dice specification [N]dM, N 1..10, M 2..100; d66 is refused.

Epigraph.description: The quoted title and flavour sentence that head a company's rules. Flavour, not a rule.

text.description: The flavour sentence after the quote.

Exchange.description: A rule models of the company swap for another.

Exempt.description: A unit or an item that does not count towards some limits.

item.description: The item exempted; this or unit.

limits.description: The ids of the limits[] it does not count towards.

unit.description: The unit exempted; this or item.

gains.description: The ways to earn Experience; a match input field exists for each key.

note.description: A note shown with the list.

amount.description: The Experience Points the gain is worth.

dice.description: A die rolled for the amount instead of a fixed one.

key.description: The key of the gain; unique.

repeatable.description: true: it can be earned several times in one match (a count is entered).

Fallback.description: Lets a recruit that would break a limit take another result.

anyRoll.description: true: any roll may be taken.

charts.description: The charts the replacement result is taken from: reinforcements, specialChart.

swapRollOn.description: The chart whose roll is swapped.

unit.description: The unit the exception is for.

FollowerRules.description: How many creatures a hero keeps, or how many wanderers a company has at once.

attachTo.description: Creatures: the roles that may have one: leader, sergeant.

maxAtOnce.description: Wanderers: the most in the company at once.

Followers.description: The rules of creatures or wanderers.

Gear.description: An item: wargear, equipment, a creature or a wanderer. In a company's gear[] it is that company's unique wargear.

abilities.description: The typed abilities the engine reads.

aftermathEffect.description: A consumable of the aftermath: the key of the campaign.aftermathEffects entry it activates.

aka.description: Other spellings of the same name (true synonyms only). A spelling that already is a vanilla name is refused.

base.description: The generic item this one is a version of.

classes.description: What the item is, from the closed set; the first is the main class. Derived from type when the type says it.

definition.description: The item text shown on its tooltip. Default: the vanilla item's text.

extends.description: An item of this file whose fields this one inherits where it does not write them; a list or object you write replaces the base's. name, definition, note and tts are never inherited.

gold.description: The Gold cost; default the rating.

grantsForChosenWeapon.description: The rule granted for one chosen weapon.

grantsSlots.description: Slots the item adds (the Backpack: 3 small).

id.description: A stable id; default: the name as a slug. Write it only to keep an id when the name changes.

kind.description: wargear, equipment, creature or wanderer. A new item needs one; an entry without a kind annotates a vanilla item.

limit.description: The most models of the company that may carry it; 0 or absent: no limit.

mount.description: A mount: the vanilla entry that holds its stat block, when it is not the item's own name.

name.description: The name of the item. Identity is the name and nothing else: equal stats, class or price never make two items one.

note.description: A note for the people who read the file; the app may show it next to the entry.

overrides.description: true when this entry deliberately replaces a lower-layer entry (vanilla or the glossary) of the same name. Without it, defining a name that already exists is an error.

pricedAs.description: Sold at the price, size and restrictions of this item (Elven-made weaponry: its generic equivalent).

profile.description: Creatures and wanderers: their profile (unit type, stats, rules, companyFeature...). Free-form.

ranged.description: The missile profile of a bow, crossbow, throwing weapon or missile.

rating.description: The rating: one number, or {warrior, hero}.

related.description: Related but distinct items (Elf Bow and Longbow share a profile).

requiresMount.description: true: only a mounted model can use it (Lance, Barding).

size.description: small or large: the slot an equipment item takes.

statChanges.description: Characteristics the item changes. With a condition it is only a note.

tts.description: The Tabletop Simulator figure of a wanderer, creature or fighting mount.

type.description: The vanilla type, from which the classes are derived (mount, bow, armour, shield, banner, spear...).

unsold.description: true: defined for its classes and text, but no armoury sells it.

who.description: Who may buy it. On a company's unique wargear: the models that may take it.

GearTTS.description: The Tabletop Simulator figure of an item.

alternatives.description: Other models that stand in as well.

model.description: The figure to spawn, "Name" or "Name: options".

name.description: The name the mod knows the item by, when it differs.

Granted.description: A special rule the company gives some of its models for free.

cost.description: The rating it adds, if any.

who.description: The models that get it; none: every model of the company.

HeroGain.description: The Might, Will and Fate a new hero starts with.

HeroProgress.description: The hero progression: the dice rolled and how many results the player keeps.

choose.description: How many of the rolled results the player keeps; at most rollsPerProgression.

roll.description: The die of a path table (a path may name its own).

rollsPerProgression.description: How many results are rolled for one level-up.

HeroRating.description: How a hero is rated: the Rating of each point of a characteristic, of each special rule and minor special rule, and when its gear is paid at the hero rating. A number that is absent is 0.

maxMinorSpecialRuleRating.description: The most the minor special rules of one hero add together.

perMinorSpecialRule.description: The Rating of each minor special rule of a hero (a rule with minor: true).

perPoint.description: The Rating of one point of each characteristic; a characteristic that is not listed adds nothing.

perSpecialRule.description: The Rating of each special rule of a hero.

wargear.description: When a hero pays the hero rating for gear.

HeroTreatment.description: One way to treat a hero: an attempt on a die (attempt) or sending the hero to the healers (healers).

healable.description: The injuries (keys of the hero chart) the method can remove.

key.description: attempt (a roll to remove an injury) or healers (no roll: the hero misses the next game).

maxAttempts.description: The most attempts allowed; null for no limit. Informational; the app puts no limit.

missNextGame.description: true: the hero misses the next game.

removesInjuries.description: How many injuries the method removes.

roll.description: The roll of an attempt; null for a method with no roll.

HeroUpgrade.description: A rule a hero of the company may take instead of a rolled level-up result.

definition.description: An inline rule definition, moved into rules[] by the loader.

flavour.description: The flavour sentence printed before the rule.

name.description: The rule the upgrade gives; it must be a rule of rules[], vanilla or the glossary (or defined by definition here).

note.description: A note for the people who read the file; the app may show it next to the entry.

who.description: The models that may take it; none: any hero.

Heroes.description: Who may be a starting hero and what a recruit that joins as a hero gets.

noStartGain.description: Starting units that keep their own Might, Will and Fate when made heroes.

recruitAsHero.description: Every recruit joins as a Hero in the Making with these gains.

who.description: The starting units that may be made heroes. Only units and except count: the starting units are chosen by name.

Included.description: A unit a bundled unit is made of, with the points it is worth.

Influence.description: The Influence a company earns after a match.

gains.description: The Influence earned after a match.

spend.description: What Influence buys, as free player-facing prose and data (a list of {key, name, text, ...}). Genuinely open: the app does not read or print it.

InfluenceGains.description: The Influence of the War's Aftermath.

participating.description: Influence for taking part in a match.

Injuries.description: The injury charts, the die they are rolled on and the treatments. The chart rows and the treatments are read by the engine; the prose keys (applies, deathOfAHero, healing, retirement, rollModifier) are rule text for the players.

applies.description: Who rolls on the charts. Prose shown to the players.

deathOfAHero.description: What happens when a Leader is slain. Prose shown to the players.

healing.description: How injuries are healed. Prose shown to the players.

retirement.description: Forced retirement. Prose; the count is the row's retireAtCount.

roll.description: The injury die, such as 2d6. Both charts must cover its totals exactly once.

rollModifier.description: Modifiers of the injury roll. Prose; the modifier is a campaign.aftermathEffects entry.

InjuryChange.description: A characteristic an injury changes: a gain on a row that is not a persistent injury, a loss (per count) on one.

amount.description: The change, a positive gain or a negative loss.

capAtPathMaximum.description: true: the gain stops at the maximum of the hero's path. Informational; the app does not read it.

minimum.description: The lowest value the characteristic may reach; null for no floor. Informational; the app does not read it.

per.description: count: the amount is applied once per time the hero has the injury.

permanent.description: true: the change stays for good. Informational; a row that is not persistent always keeps its gain.

raisesPathMaximum.description: true: the gain also raises the path's maximum. Informational; the app does not read it.

InjuryDisable.description: What a lasting injury takes from a hero: the benefit of gear of some classes or by name, or an ability.

classes.description: The gear classes, for kind gearClass.

key.description: The ability, for kind ability: standFast or heroicActionsOnCompany.

kind.description: gearClass (items of the listed classes give no benefit), gearItem (the named items give none) or ability (the hero loses the ability).

names.description: The item names, for kind gearItem.

InjuryHealingText.description: The rulebook text of how injuries are healed. Prose; the app does not read it.

InjuryHeals.description: What a healing result removes: injuries of the listed keys, chosen by the player.

choice.description: Who chooses the injury healed: player.

keys.description: The keys of the hero injuries that can be healed.

InjuryReroll.description: The optional second roll of T'is Just a Scratch.

ifScratchAgainMissNextGame.description: true: a second result of the same row means the hero misses the next game.

optional.description: true: the player chooses whether to roll again.

secondResultStands.description: true: the second result applies even if it is worse than the first.

InjuryRetirement.description: What happens to a hero that suffers a persistent injury for the retireAtCount-th time. Prose; the count is the row's retireAtCount.

result.description: The key of the chart row a forced retirement counts as (dead).

InjuryRollModifier.description: The rulebook text about modifiers of the injury roll (Healing Herbs). Prose; the modifier itself is a campaign.aftermathEffects entry.

appliesTo.description: What the modifier is added to: total2d6, the total of the injury dice.

clamp.description: [low, high]: the modified total is kept inside these bounds.

includesRerolls.description: true: the modifier also applies to a re-roll.

replacedBy.description: Where the modifier is defined, for the reader of the file.

InjuryRow.description: A row of an injury chart. The engine reads effects (remove, missNextGame, fullRecovery) to decide what the result does, and persistent, retireAtCount, statChanges, disables and grantsAtCount for a hero's lasting injuries.

cancelsMissedGame.description: true: the result cancels the missed next game.

clearsAfterGames.description: The injury ends after this many games.

disables.description: What a lasting injury takes from the hero.

effects.description: What the result does. remove (the model dies), missNextGame and fullRecovery decide the result; the others (healOneInjury, reduceMovement, noShield...) label the effect for the reader and are done by the other keys of the row.

experience.description: The die of grantsExperience in the rulebook's words (D3). The app reads grantsExperience.

grantsAtCount.description: Special rules the hero gets from a count of the injury on: {"2": {specialRule}}.

grantsExperience.description: Experience rolled on a die when the result comes up.

grantsInfluence.description: Influence rolled on a die for the company when the result comes up.

healable.description: true: a treatment can remove the injury.

healableBy.description: The treatment methods that can remove the injury (a key of campaign.injuries.treatment.hero), for a status such as T'is Just a Scratch.

heals.description: The injuries a healing result removes.

influence.description: The die of grantsInfluence in the rulebook's words (D6). The app reads grantsInfluence.

key.description: The key the engine switches on (dead, injured, fullRecovery...). A row with no effects is read by its key: dead, injured, else a full recovery.

optionalReroll.description: true: the player may roll again on the chart instead of taking the result (T'is Just a Scratch).

persistent.description: true: the hero keeps the injury and counts how often it suffered it (arm wound, leg wound, broken honour).

reroll.description: How the re-roll of an optionalReroll result works.

retireAtCount.description: A persistent injury forces the hero to retire at this count, as the Dead result.

roll.description: The roll or range the row covers.

stat.description: The characteristics changed, as {characteristic: change}, for the reader of the file. The app reads statChanges.

statChanges.description: The characteristics the result changes (a gain on a row that is not a persistent injury, a loss on one).

stat_note.description: A note on stat, for the reader of the file.

text.description: The rule text of the result.

InjuryTreatment.description: How Influence treats injuries (Battle Companies, Step 3): the hero methods, the warrior's and what removing an injury does.

currency.description: What a treatment costs: influence. Informational; the app spends Influence.

hero.description: The hero treatments. The engine knows attempt and healers.

phase.description: When a treatment is made: companyManagement. Informational.

removalEffect.description: What removing an injury does to the hero's counts.

InputField.description: One thing the players enter, per company or per model.

computed.description: true: the app works it out; nobody enters it.

computedFrom.description: What it is worked out from.

default.description: The starting value: true or false for a flag, a number for a count, the chosen word for an enum. Open data.

experience.description: The key of the experience gain (campaign.experience.gains) it records.

feeds.description: What the field feeds: influence, experience, rerolls, rewards, itemUse, breakPoint, injuries.

inferred.description: What follows from the field, for the reader of the file.

key.description: The key of the field; unique in its list.

maxPerCompany.description: The most models of one company that can have it.

min.description: The lowest number that can be entered.

optional.description: true: the field may stay empty.

options.description: The words to choose from, as a list, or the path of the table they come from. Open data.

text.description: What the players enter, in words.

type.description: How it is entered: enum or select (one of the options), multiSelect (several), integer, count, flag (yes or no), flags, scoringObjectives.

when.description: When the field is asked for.

KeywordLimit.description: Caps the share of a company that may have a keyword.

percent.description: The most, as a percent of the company, converted to the exact fraction over 100 (Helm's Deep: 33 is 33/100). Write this or share.

share.description: The most, as a share of the company: a fraction like "1/3". Write this or percent.

Limit.description: A company-wide limit on a class of items or a keyword (no more than a share of the company may carry it).

id.description: The id a company's limits refer to.

maximumPercentage.description: The most, as a percent of the company (0.01 to 100), converted to the exact fraction over 100 (33.33 is 3333/10000, not 1/3: write share). Write this or share.

share.description: The most, as a share of the company: a fraction like "1/3". Write this or maximumPercentage.

value.description: For a keyword limit, the keyword.

Magic.description: What Battle Companies says about magical powers.

floor.description: A casting value is never improved below this (2 is 2+); default 1. No power may be cast below it.

listed.description: Vanilla powers Battle Companies lists though nobody learns them.

maxPerPower.description: Improvements of one power per hero; default 1.

powers.description: The powers by name: each a vanilla power the file gives a range and casting value.

MatchAftermath.description: The order in which the War's Aftermath is applied.

order.description: The steps of the aftermath, in order: injuries, experience, progression, influence.

rewards.description: Where the scenario rewards come from and when they apply.

MatchGold.description: What the rulebook says about Gold in a scenario.

MatchInput.description: What the players enter per match, described for the people who read the file. The app builds its match forms from its own tables (the experience gains, the scenarios, Against the Odds) and does not read this description.

gold.description: What the rulebook says about Gold in a scenario.

perCompany.description: What is entered for each company.

perModel.description: What is entered for each model.

text.description: What the players enter, in words.

MatchResult.description: How the winner of a match is decided.

decidedBy.description: victoryPoints: the company with the most Victory Points wins.

outcomes.description: The results a match can have: win, draw, loss.

tie.description: What equal Victory Points are: draw.

NoPromotion.description: What a warrior whose promotion roll finds no promotion gains instead.

courage.description: The Courage improvement (a lower Courage number is better).

maximum.description: The best value (as a number, 3 for 3+) the improvement may reach.

Nomination.description: What a player notes down at the start for a secret objective.

allowLeader.description: onlyHero: the Leader may be picked only when the company has a single Hero. Heroes only.

where.description: opponentHalf: a terrain piece wholly in the opponent's half. Terrain only.

Oath.description: The oath the player swears when taking command of the company.

text.description: The oath. {name} stands exactly once, not at the start or the end, where the company's name goes.

vow.description: The label of the button the player presses (1 to 40 characters).

Oaths.description: The fallback oaths of the companies that have none of their own, one per alignment.

evil.description: The oath of an evil company.

good.description: The oath of a good company.

OptionException.description: An option the notSold words would hide, or that is read as another item.

granted.description: true: the model comes with it from the charts or the starting company.

ownItem.description: An item of its own that no armoury sells, choosable under its own name.

reason.description: Why it is not sold; the armoury shows it.

OptionSwap.description: The path an option puts in the place of another path (a house rule that swaps one path for another).

OwnPath.description: The units that are On Their Own Path.

path.description: The path they follow; default On Their Own Path.

units.description: The units that are On Their Own Path.

Parameter.description: Says a rule takes a bracketed argument, such as Hatred (X).

kind.description: What the X is: keyword, weapon, rollTarget, number or companyHero.

Path.description: A heroic path: how a hero levels up, as a table keyed by a roll.

aka.description: Other spellings of the same name (true synonyms only). A spelling that already is a vanilla name is refused.

description.description: A short description shown to the players.

dice.description: The dice of the path table; default campaign.progression.hero.roll. The rows must cover them exactly once.

extends.description: A path of this file whose fields (rows, maximums...) this one inherits where it does not write them.

heroicAction.description: The name of the Heroic Action the path starts with, or null when it adds none. Its text is the rule's.

id.description: A stable id; default: the name as a slug. Write it only to keep an id when the name changes.

kind.description: heroic (default): offered to heroes. custom: the homebrew path an option hands out, hidden. endOfPath: no table, only rule.

limit.description: The most heroes of a company that may take the path (the Sorcerer: 1).

mastery.description: The name of the Mastery rule.

maximums.description: The ceilings per characteristic, as {stat: {max, maxIncrease, best}}: max is the highest value the stat may reach, maxIncrease the most points level-ups may add to the profile, best the best (lowest) value of a stat where lower is better, such as 3 for Courage 3+. They apply together with the overall peak.

note.description: A note for the people who read the file; the app may show it next to the entry.

rows.description: The table, one row per roll.

rule.description: The rule of an endOfPath path (At Path's End).

spells.description: The magical powers of the path (names).

start.description: Might, Will and Fate a model starts on the path with, when it is not the usual hero start.

PathOption.description: A closed alternative of a path result: exactly one of stat, rule, minorRule, heroicAction, power, castingValue, oneOf or one of the open choices anyMinorRule, anyHeroicAction and anyPower is set.

anyHeroicAction.description: A Heroic Action the hero does not have yet, its choice.

anyMinorRule.description: A minor special rule of the minor list, the hero's choice.

anyPower.description: A magical power of the path's spells the hero does not know yet, its choice.

castingValue.description: Improves a casting value by this much.

max.description: The highest the stat may reach through this result.

maxTotal.description: The most such results a hero can take in total.

oneOf.description: The hero picks one of these.

rollAgain.description: The hero also takes its other result.

rule.description: Gives this special rule: a name, or a rule definition written here.

PathRow.description: The result of one roll on a path.

options.description: The alternatives of the result; the engine offers each.

text.description: The text of the row. Derived when absent; write it only when it cannot be derived.

PeakLimits.description: The overall limit of each characteristic (one key per characteristic, only those that have one), and the Will maximum some paths have of their own.

willMaxOverrides.description: The Will maximum a path has of its own, by path name (1..10); it replaces the peak's Will maximum for heroes of that path.

Pin.description: Records which occurrence of a name that vanilla defines twice is meant. Without a pin the first wins.

kind.description: hero, warrior, unit, item, rule or mount.

occurrence.description: Which occurrence is meant, counting from 1.

Power.description: The range and casting value Battle Companies gives a vanilla power.

auras.description: The rings the power draws while in effect.

casting.description: The Casting Value a hero learns it at, such as 4+.

Progression.description: Experience, level-ups and the dice of the warrior and hero progression.

threshold.description: Experience Points per level-up: a model rolls floor(XP / threshold) times and nothing is spent.

Promotion.description: What happens to a unit of the company that rolls a promotion or a Hero in the Making.

forgo.description: true: the player may keep the unit as it is.

on.description: The progression result: noChange, promoted or heroInTheMaking.

statGain.description: true: it also gains the Might, Will and Fate of a new hero.

Ranged.description: The missile profile of an item.

RareRule.description: Which models of a profile count towards its Rare N limit.

deadCount.description: true: a dead model counts towards Rare N.

injuredCount.description: true: an injured model counts towards Rare N.

promotedCount.description: true: a model that was promoted to another profile still counts for its old profile.

Rating.description: A rating: one number for warrior and hero alike, or {warrior, hero}.

RatingPoint.description: The Rating one point of a characteristic is worth in a hero.

rating.description: The Rating of one point of it.

RatingRules.description: How companies and heroes are rated.

Recruit.description: The recruitment exceptions of a company.

fallback.description: A recruit that would break a limit takes another result.

Recruitment.description: How reinforcements are rolled: the die, how Influence moves the die, and which models count towards a Rare limit.

die.description: The recruiting die: one die, written dN. Every reinforcement and special chart must cover 1..N exactly once.

rare.description: Which models count towards a Rare N limit.

Replace.description: A recruit that may be swapped: a unit that takes an officer's place once the company's one is slain, or an alternative offered on some rolls of a chart.

alternative.description: For an alternative: the unit offered at no cost instead.

chart.description: For an alternative: the chart (reinforcements, specialChart).

roles.description: The officer roles it may take: leader, sergeant.

roll.description: For an alternative: the roll of that chart it replaces.

unit.description: The unit that takes the place (Shire: the Ranger of the North).

Roll.description: A chart roll: a whole number, a range "lo-hi" or a pair [lo, hi].

Rule.description: A special rule (keyword): its text, who it works against or for, the rings it draws.

aka.description: Other spellings of the same name (true synonyms only). A spelling that already is a vanilla name is refused.

bareTarget.description: The target of the rule written without its bracket (Terror: all enemies; Terror (X): the keyword). Needs parameter and target.

definition.description: The rule text, copied from the rulebook.

id.description: A stable id; default: the name as a slug. Write it only to keep an id when the name changes.

label.description: The name the pages show when the key is plainer.

minor.description: true: a minor special rule (the list a path may offer).

name.description: The name of the rule. A rule that exists in vanilla needs overrides to be redefined.

note.description: A note for the people who read the file; the app may show it next to the entry.

overrides.description: true when this entry deliberately replaces a lower-layer entry (vanilla or the glossary) of the same name. Without it, defining a name that already exists is an error.

parameter.description: Says the rule takes a bracketed argument.

target.description: Who it works against or for.

RuleRef.description: A rule name, or a rule definition object that the loader hoists.

Scalar.description: A string or a number read as text (the rulebook version).

Scenario.description: A scenario: its text sections, special rules and Victory Point objectives.

aka.description: Other spellings of the same name (true synonyms only). A spelling that already is a vanilla name is refused.

description.description: A short description shown to the players.

id.description: A stable id; default: the name as a slug. Write it only to keep an id when the name changes.

name.description: The name of the scenario; the key the selection tables list.

objectives.description: The Objectives section (how the game ends).

outline.description: The short lead-in some scenarios print before the description.

rewards.description: A list of {effect, name, text, who, condition}; effect is a key of campaign.aftermathEffects. Not typed.

roles.description: A list of {key, name}, such as attacker and defender.

scoring.description: The Victory Point objectives, one per printed bullet, in printed order.

specialRules.description: A list of {name, definition, table?}; a table is {lookup, columns, rows[{min, max, cells}]}. Not typed.

usesRules.description: Rules applied without text of their own, shown by name.

ScenarioSelection.description: How the scenario of a match is rolled: a first die picks a table, a second die picks the scenario in it.

die.description: The first die: one die, written dN. The ranges of tables partition 1..N and each table lists N scenarios.

tables.description: The tables; the first die picks one, the second picks the scenario in it.

ScenarioTable.description: One table of scenarios, picked by the first die.

roll.description: The roll or range of the first die that picks this table.

scenarios.description: Exactly N scenario names, one per face of the second die; each must be a scenarios[] name.

Scoring.description: One scoring objective of a scenario: the sentences that award Victory Points.

count.description: For each / eachTiers: how many items.

instruction.description: The note-down sentence of a secret objective.

item.description: For each / eachTiers: what is counted.

key.description: A key unique within the scenario.

kind.description: tiers (the best tier reached), each (item times pointsEach up to count), eachTiers (every item scores its own best tier).

options.description: The printed sentences with their points.

secret.description: true: kept hidden until the end of the game.

ScoringOption.description: A tier of a scoring objective: its sentence and the Victory Points.

Share.description: A share as an integer fraction "1/3" (numerator 0.., denominator 1..1000000, at most 1), or a number, which is a percent converted to the exact fraction over 100 (50 is 1/2, 66 is 33/50).

SlotPair.description: A number of small and of large equipment slots.

Slots.description: Small and large equipment slots an item adds to its bearer.

SpecialChart.description: The special units chart, and the units a company may buy directly.

buy.description: Units bought directly for their own cost.

rows.description: The rows; together they cover the recruiting die exactly once.

Start.description: The starting force of a company.

gold.description: The Gold the company starts with.

StartUnit.description: One line of the starting force.

role.description: The place the company suggests for it: leader, sergeant or heroInTheMaking. None for a plain warrior.

unit.description: The name the company calls the unit: a vanilla unit, or an own unit of the company or of units[].

with.description: The options or wargear the model starts with.

StatChange.description: A characteristic changed by an item.

condition.description: If set, the change holds only under this condition, so it is a note and is never added to the profile.

StatLimit.description: How far one characteristic may be improved. A key that is absent sets no limit of that kind. The same shape is used by the overall peak and by a path's maximums.

best.description: The best (lowest) value of a characteristic where lower is better.

max.description: The highest value of a characteristic where higher is better.

maxIncrease.description: The most points level-ups may add to the profile (without gear).

SubTarget.description: The model that is treated as another: a role of the company, or any hero with a rule.

withRule.description: Only a hero with this rule.

Substitution.description: Models of the company treat some model as another for a rule (the Leader counts as Faramir for Loyal to the Captain).

appliesTo.description: The rule the substitution is for.

target.description: The model that is treated as another.

treatedAs.description: The model it is treated as.

TableRow.description: A row of the warrior progression table.

key.description: The key the engine switches on.

roll.description: The roll or range the row covers.

text.description: The rule text of the result.

Target.description: Who a rule works against or for.

bearerKeywords.description: The rule only works while the bearer has one of these keywords.

keywords.description: The keywords the rule is about.

match.description: any (default) or all of the keywords.

text.description: In words, who it works against or for.

TotalCap.description: The most Courage and Intelligence may be improved in total from the unmodified profile.

includesGear.description: true: the improvement from gear counts in the total.

value.description: The most points, 1..10, Courage and Intelligence may be improved in total.

costKept.description: true: the Influence is lost on a failure.

effect.description: none: a failure has no other effect.

TreatModifier.description: How extra Influence raises a treatment roll, like a Might point.

ceiling.description: The raised roll never goes above this; 0 for no ceiling. At least the target.

like.description: What the modifier resembles in the rulebook (a Might point).

maxPoints.description: The most extra points allowed; null for no limit. Informational; the ceiling limits the roll.

perPoint.description: The roll gained per extra Influence point.

TreatRoll.description: The die of a treatment attempt: the total must reach the target, and extra Influence raises it.

compare.description: gte: the total must be at least the target.

modifier.description: How extra Influence raises the roll.

naturalMaxIsAlwaysEnough.description: true: the highest roll always succeeds. Informational; the app does not read it.

target.description: The total the roll must reach; a total the dice can show.

TreatmentRemoval.description: What removing an injury does to the hero's counts.

choice.description: Who chooses the injury removed: player.

countDelta.description: The change of the injury's count (-1).

derivedEffects.description: recomputeFromCounts: the effects of the injuries follow from the counts.

TypeDelta.description: Unit types added to and removed from a unit.

Unit.description: A unit entry. Three forms: an annotation of a lower-layer unit (the name of a vanilla unit plus properties, no definition), a unit built on another with extends and deltas, or a brand-new unit with a full definition and no base.

addRules.description: Special rules added at no cost.

aka.description: Other spellings of the same name (true synonyms only). A spelling that already is a vanilla name is refused.

composite.description: Makes the unit one model that counts as several.

extends.description: The unit this one is built on: a vanilla unit (its profile is used), or a unit of this file (its fields are inherited where not written). Omit for an annotation or a brand-new unit.

id.description: A stable id; default: the name as a slug. Write it only to keep an id when the name changes.

includes.description: The units this one is made of, with their points.

models.description: How many models a recruit counts as against the company maximum.

name.description: The name of the unit. Default: the name in extends (an annotation).

note.description: The sentence the card prints to explain what the unit is.

options.description: A brand-new unit: what it may take, as the vanilla file writes its options: a list of {name, points} (and chooseOneKey / requireChooseOneKey for a choose-one group).

overrides.description: true when this entry deliberately replaces a lower-layer entry (vanilla or the glossary) of the same name. Without it, defining a name that already exists is an error.

ownPath.description: Marks the unit as On Their Own Path.

points.description: A brand-new unit: its points cost.

profile.description: A brand-new unit: its full profile, written the way the vanilla file writes one: the characteristics movement, fight, shoot ("-" for none), strength, defence, attack, wounds, courage, intelligence (and might, will, fate for a hero), and the lists race, unitType (both required), faction, specialRules, wargear, heroicActions, magicalPowers and baseSize. The app then treats the unit like a vanilla profile.

with.description: The options of the base unit that are pre-selected (Tookish Hunter = Hobbit Archer with the Bow option).

UnitTTS.description: The Tabletop Simulator figure of a unit.

alternatives.description: Other models the mod has for the unit.

defaultOptions.description: The options the unit is requested with when it carries none.

foot.description: A cavalry unit: the rider on foot, a vanilla unit.

marker.description: An alias marker option left out of the key when it is the unit's only option.

model.description: The model the mod knows the unit by, when it differs from the unit's name.

options.description: Option spellings that differ between the vanilla file and the mod.

states.description: A cavalry unit: every model of it in the mod carries the state that dismounts the figure.

Vanilla.description: What Battle Companies says about vanilla things: which duplicate wins, what a vanilla unit lacks, which options are not sold.

mounts.description: Fill-ins for vanilla mounts, by name.

pins.description: The occurrence of a duplicated vanilla name that wins.

units.description: Fill-ins for vanilla units, by name.

VanillaFill.description: Fields a vanilla unit or mount lacks; applied only where the vanilla field is empty.

exceptions.description: The few options the words would hide or that are read as another item.

notSold.description: Words: a vanilla option whose name contains one is not sold (banner, war horn, war drum).

reason.description: Why those words are not sold; the armoury shows it.

WargearRating.description: When a hero pays the hero rating for its gear.

WargearThreshold.description: A hero whose listed characteristics add up to at least sumAtLeast pays the hero rating for its wargear.

sumAtLeast.description: The sum at which the hero rating applies.

WarriorProgress.description: The warrior progression: the die, its table and what a warrior with no promotion gains.

noPromotion.description: What a warrior with no promotion gains.

roll.description: The die of the warrior table; its rows must cover it exactly once.

table.description: The rows of the warrior table. Keys noChange, promoted and heroInTheMaking are the ones the engine knows.

WarriorTreatment.description: The treatment of a warrior: the cost in Influence of removing the Injured condition.

requires.description: injured: what the warrior must have.

roll.description: null: a warrior is treated without a roll.

WhenBroken.description: What happens to a Broken company.

courageTest.description: The Courage test of a Broken company.

Who.description: The one selector of "which models": every field narrows it, all that are set must hold, and an empty selector admits every model.

alignment.description: good or evil: the alignment of the company.

except.description: Exact unit names that are left out.

hero.description: true: heroes only; false: warriors only.

keywords.description: Any of these keywords of the model: its races, factions and unit types, or Cavalry for a model that rides.

race.description: Any of these races (Elf, Hobbit). A model whose profile is unknown is not refused.

refusal.description: Display only: what the armoury says to a model that is not admitted. Made from the fields when empty.

text.description: Display only: how the page names the models. Made from the fields when empty.

units.description: Exact unit names (the name of the model or of its profile), never part of a name.

description: The whole Battle Companies file: a header, the campaign engine parameters and the sections of rules, items, paths, scenarios, companies and units. The file is complete, not a patch: it is uploaded as the Battle Companies file of a ruleset next to the vanilla file and the glossary. Generated from internal/core/lean/model.go and campaign.go by `go test ./internal/core/lean -run TestSchemaUpToDate -update-schema`; never edit by hand. The Go decoder (lean.Decode) is the authority: it also checks names, charts and cross references, which a schema cannot.

auras.description: The vocabulary tables of the auras: kinds and groups.

creatures.description: The rules of creatures (Baggage Pony, Falcon...).

credit.description: Who wrote the rules this file transcribes: a list of {name, author, version}. Informational; the app does not read it.

extends.description: The name of the vanilla file the ruleset is played with, such as "Middle-Earth Strategy Battle Game - 2024". Write it: the upload uses this key to recognise a Battle Companies file (the checker alone does not need it). The file is not merged with anything.

gear.description: The items: wargear, equipment, creatures and wanderers, plus annotations of vanilla items.

limits.description: The company-wide limits on classes of items or keywords (bows, throwing weapons, Cavalry).

magic.description: Magical powers: casting limits and the range and casting value of each power.

name.description: The name of the ruleset as the admin page and the campaign form list it.

rules.description: The special rules (keywords) that Battle Companies defines or annotates, each defined once and named everywhere else.

schemaVersion.description: The format version. It must be 2; a file without it, or of another version, is refused with one message.

units.description: Units shared by every company: annotations of vanilla units, or units built on one.

vanilla.description: What the file says about vanilla things: pins of duplicate names, fill-ins, unsold options.

version.description: The version of the ruleset, a string such as "1.1" (a number is read as text). With the name and the short hash it tells two uploads apart.

title: Battle Companies rules file, lean format (schemaVersion 2)
